project.title: Temporal progression of the depurative capacity of enhanced Soil Aquifer Treatments. Role of microbial communities.
project.description: Soil Aquifer Treatment (SAT) systems represent a cost-efficient and nature-based solution for water reclamation, with strong potential to reduce biological and chemical hazards from Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) effluents. These systems typically achieve over 95 percent removal of bacterial loads, antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), recalcitrant contaminants of emerging concern (CECs), and toxic activities (for example, estrogenic and dioxin-like responses). In this study, we evaluate the time evolution of the depurative efficiency of two pilot SAT systems recharging the same WWTP secondary effluent. One of them contains a reactive barrier -consisting of sand, woodchips, compost, biochar, zeolites, and clay- and the other one does not. We monitored CECs, microbial communities, ARGs, and toxicity over six recharge episodes during a two-year period. The results showed that operational efficiency increased over time, with orders of magnitude reductions bacterial loads and ARGs, and toxicity after approximately one year of operation, coinciding with the establishment of bacterial populations exhibiting metabolic capacities distinct from the copiotrophic, fermentative groups predominant in the WWTP effluent microbiota. The rate of improvement in terms of CECs was not as dramatic, but kept improving as the microbiota kept adapting to the WWTP effluent. The presence of the reactive barrier was improved CECs removal, but not so much toxicity or microbial indicators. These results have important practical implications: for monitoring and for construction of SAT systems, as the indicate that prior inoculation of new materials with microbial communities from mature systems could accelerate functional stabilization. These findings have relevant implications for understanding the functioning of SAT systems and optimizing their implementation for safe and sustainable water reclamation.
